subsystems.name: Prospecting and survey
subsystems.role: find asteroids and work out what they contain before committing to a mission.

subsystems.name: Rendezvous and anchoring
subsystems.role: hold position against near-zero gravity, where you cannot simply land and drill using weight.

subsystems.name: Extraction and volatile capture
subsystems.role: release water and other volatiles from the rock and collect them as gas or ice.

subsystems.name: Material separation
subsystems.role: split the processed material into water, metals and waste.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: run processing far from the Sun, where sunlight is weak and heat is hard to dump.

subsystems.name: Storage and transfer
subsystems.role: keep water or propellant cold and hand it over to a customer spacecraft.

subsystems.name: Autonomy and control
subsystems.role: operate where radio signals take many minutes to arrive, so remote joystick control is impossible.

buildSteps.title: Survey candidate asteroids
buildSteps.detail: Telescope surveys in the infrared find near-Earth asteroids, and spectroscopy gives a rough idea of whether they look water-rich (C-type) or metal-rich (M-type).

buildSteps.title: Characterise a target up close
buildSteps.detail: A small spacecraft rendezvouses, maps surface structure, measures gravity and takes spectra to confirm the composition the telescope suggested.

buildSteps.title: Prove the process on the ground
buildSteps.detail: Meteorites and simulated asteroid material are heated in vacuum chambers to measure how much water and gas comes off, at what temperature, and how the residue separates.

buildSteps.title: Fly a small extraction demonstration
buildSteps.detail: A spacecraft touches or anchors to a small body, seals a few hundred grams of material in a chamber, heats it and captures the released water vapour. This step has never been done.

buildSteps.title: Solve anchoring and reaction forces
buildSteps.detail: Cutting or drilling pushes back; with almost no gravity the spacecraft must be held down by thrusters, a harpoon or a bag that wraps the rock, and this is tested in microgravity.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a pilot plant
buildSteps.detail: Processing moves from grams to tonnes per visit, which demands far more power, bigger tanks and fully autonomous operation under long signal delays.

buildSteps.title: Store and deliver the product
buildSteps.detail: Water is kept as ice or cryogenic liquid in tanks and docked to a depot or customer spacecraft; transfer of cryogenic fluids in microgravity is still barely demonstrated.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop economically
buildSteps.detail: The first sales are almost certainly propellant to spacecraft already in space rather than metal shipped to Earth, where mined metal would be far cheaper.

prerequisites.why: launch costs have fallen, but sending mass to a near-Earth asteroid and back is still far more expensive than any product delivered on Earth.
spacecraft have touched and sampled asteroids, but sustained drilling, crushing and holding of machinery has not been shown.
laboratory heating of meteorites and simulated regolith yields water and gases, but nothing has been run in space at useful scale.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic storage and transfer in microgravity
prerequisites.why: without it, harvested water cannot be kept or handed to customers.

prerequisites.tech: In-space demand for propellant and materials
prerequisites.why: the business case needs many customers in orbit willing to buy water-derived propellant rather than launch it from Earth.
signal delays of minutes to tens of minutes rule out ground control of delicate mining operations.

pathway.milestone: prospecting and sample return: Hayabusa2 returned material from Ryugu in 2020 and OSIRIS-REx from Bennu in 2023
pathway.unlocks: hard data on asteroid composition, structure and how to touch one safely.

pathway.milestone: dedicated prospecting missions to several near-Earth asteroids, plus Hera's survey of the Didymos system from 2026
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of accessible, water-rich targets with known hazards.

pathway.milestone: an in-space demonstration that extracts, stores and transfers a small amount of water
pathway.unlocks: proof the value chain works end to end, not just in a laboratory.

pathway.milestone: a pilot operation processing tonnes of material per visit and selling propellant in orbit
pathway.unlocks: a genuine off-world supply industry; metals for orbital construction only follow if that market grows.
